column1: # pgrdf.surface() manifest — authored classification of every export.
# Classes: stable (contract; removal/signature change = breaking release)
#          internal (reachable but not API; no compatibility promise)
#          spike (development measurement harness; may vanish without notice)
#          deprecated (superseded; the note names the replacement)
# Notes are CONSUMER-FACING: they describe what the function is and how to
# use it well, in words that stand alone. A completeness test enforces this
# file covers every extension-owned function in both directions.
_path_walk(preds bigint[], graph_id bigint, seed bigint, follow_inverse boolean, max_depth integer, path_id integer, per_graph boolean)
column3: the breadth-first walk behind SPARQL + and * property paths (visited set per start, exact depth truncation, memory budget pgrdf.path_max_pairs); called by translated SQL, not an API. Since 0.6.37

column1: _nt_line(style integer, graph_id bigint, s_id bigint, s_type smallint, s_value text, p_id bigint, p_value text, o_id bigint, o_type smallint, o_value text, o_datatype text, o_language text)
column3: one stored triple as one line, the row formatter behind export_graph, graph_manifest, graph_digest and structural_digest: PostgreSQL sorts its output, so those functions hold a batch of lines instead of the graph. Refuses 22021 on a term containing U+0000. Not an API. Since 0.6.41
trigger function lock_graph installs on a locked graph's partition: refuses direct SQL INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE with 55P03 and the unlock cure as HINT. Not callable as an API. Since 0.6.37
ensures the quad partition for a raw graph id; consumers create graphs by IRI with add_graph(iri)
binds an explicit id/IRI pair; refuses rebinding either side. Consumers create graphs by IRI

create (or ensure) a graph by IRI; returns its graph_id; idempotent. Ids are never reused (since 0.6.39): the IRI is the identity, the id a handle. Creating a new graph needs SELECT and INSERT on pgrdf._pgrdf_quads and pgrdf._pgrdf_graphs (42501 otherwise, HINT names the grant); the partition DDL itself runs as the storage owner. Since 0.6.37
which build of version() this binary is (git describe at compile time); 'unknown' means the build did not supply one. Since 0.6.29
can the current role clear graphs? true when it holds SELECT and DELETE on pgrdf._pgrdf_quads, the exact rule clear_graph enforces. Since 0.6.38

can the current role create graphs? true when it holds SELECT and INSERT on pgrdf._pgrdf_quads and pgrdf._pgrdf_graphs, the exact rule add_graph enforces. Read this rather than inferring from table ownership. Since 0.6.37
can the current role drop graphs? true when it holds SELECT and DELETE on pgrdf._pgrdf_quads and pgrdf._pgrdf_graphs, the exact rule drop_graph enforces. Since 0.6.37

column1: carve_graph(src bigint, predicate text, dst bigint)
column3: copy the subgraph matching one predicate from src into dst Stored as a set: returns the triples dst gained, and a triple dst already holds is not stored again (since 0.6.41). Recorded as a carve act

column1: carve_graph(src bigint, seeds text[], dst bigint, max_hops integer)
column3: copy the neighbourhood reachable from seed IRIs within max_hops from src into dst Stored as a set (since 0.6.41); returns the triples dst gained. Recorded as a carve act

remove every triple from a graph; the graph itself remains. Refuses on a locked graph (55P03). Needs SELECT and DELETE on pgrdf._pgrdf_quads (42501 otherwise, HINT names the grant); the partition TRUNCATE runs as the storage owner. Since 0.6.38 Since 0.6.41 also resets the graph's source digest and materialization stamps (they described content that is gone) and is recorded as a clear act
remove every triple from a graph by IRI; unknown IRI refuses (42704)

create a NEW graph by IRI, or refuse 42710 if the IRI exists; the HINT names the existing graph_id and its recorded source digest, so a caller can reuse it or choose another IRI. Atomic against concurrent claims. Needs SELECT and INSERT on pgrdf._pgrdf_quads and pgrdf._pgrdf_graphs. add_graph(iri) stays get-or-create. Since 0.6.37
SPARQL CONSTRUCT; rows are JSONB triples suitable for put_construct_rows

copy src into dst as a set: dst gains the triples it lacks and the call returns how many that was, so a second copy returns 0 (since 0.6.41; it used to append every row again and return the source count). Carries inferred triples with it, and a triple asserted in src turns an inferred copy in dst asserted; re-materialize dst after. Recorded as a copy act
copy by IRI; same set semantics and return value as the id form
total quads (asserted + inferred) in one graph; graph 0 is the default graph
SPARQL DESCRIBE; rows are JSONB triples

drop a graph and its partition; refuses over inferred rows unless cascade (2BP01); cannot drop the default partition. Needs SELECT and DELETE on pgrdf._pgrdf_quads and pgrdf._pgrdf_graphs (42501 otherwise); the partition DDL runs as the storage owner. Since 0.6.37
drop by IRI; unknown IRI refuses (42704)
lexical value of a dictionary term id, as returned in query results and inventory

column1: graph_diff(a bigint, b bigint, side text, predicate text, class text)
column3: the triples that differ from graph a to graph b, blank-node-aware: side '-' (only in a) or '+' (only in b), terms in N-Triples form, component NULL for a ground triple else its blank-node component's rdfc-1.0 digest. Ordered side then canonical line, so OFFSET/LIMIT paging is deterministic. predicate/class narrow the comparison; a component is returned whole if any triple matches. Empty iff the graphs are isomorphic. Since 0.6.37

counts of what changed from graph a to graph b, with its method label: ground removed/added/common (triples), components removed/added/common (a multiset of rdfc-1.0 component digests) and their triples, by_predicate (ground + component triples) and by_type (rdf:type triples per class). Since 0.6.37

canonical graph identity, method rdfc-1.0-sha256: survives reload and blank-node relabelling; equal AND unequal are both conclusive. Over the SET of asserted triples: a triple the graph stores more than once counts once (since 0.6.41; a locked graph keeps the digest recorded for it). Absent graph refuses (42704); empty graph answers. Ground triples are streamed; only the triples involving a blank node are held, and past pgrdf.digest_max_bnode_quads the call refuses 54000. A graph holding a term with U+0000 refuses 22021 (see nul_term_report). Not comparable with structural_digest values. Since 0.6.32
graph_id for an IRI, or NULL when unknown — check before feeding into strict functions, which silently pass NULL through

stored terms containing U+0000 (versions before 0.6.41 could store one): one row per term with its dictionary id, type, a preview with the character written \u0000, and the ids of the graphs using it. export_graph, graph_manifest, graph_digest and structural_digest refuse such a graph (22021); the cure is to reload it from a corrected source. Reads the whole dictionary. Since 0.6.41
term-position integrity report (non-IRI predicates, literal subjects); unclean graphs validate vacuously and should be reloaded

a graph's asserted triples as canonical N-Triples, byte-sorted, one line per triple; a triple the graph stores more than once is one line (since 0.6.41); inferred rows never export (they re-derive). Streamed: backend memory does not grow with the graph. Absent graph refuses (42704); a graph holding a term with U+0000 refuses 22021 before the first line (see nul_term_report). Since 0.6.34

the graphs the caller is entitled to see, each with IRI, asserted/inferred counts, lock state, materialization freshness (current/stale/never/unknown), source_sha256 and source_loads (what the graph was loaded from; since 0.6.37), identity_digest (a locked graph's cached rdfc-1.0 digest while lock custody holds; since 0.6.37), owner (the recorded graph owner, a role name; NULL on graphs created before 0.6.41), created_at, created_workspace / created_agent / created_thread (the declared identity on the creating act) and locked_by (the role holding the current lock). Since 0.6.42 the counts come from the count the engine keeps as it writes, so the call takes milliseconds whatever the number of triples, and four columns say what the count stands on: change_seq (moves with every committed content change of the graph), counts_verified (the count was set by a scan and every change since came through the engine; a graph where it is false was counted by scan for this call, so asserted and inferred are exact either way), counts_scanned_at and last_act_id. Since 0.6.42 the listing follows the role: a superuser, a role holding the storage owner's privileges, or one holding pg_read_all_data sees every graph; any other role sees the graphs it owns, and a graph with no recorded owner is listed to admins only until pgrdf.set_graph_owner assigns it. A listing rule, not secrecy: a role that may read triples can count any graph by query. The supported alternative to reading private tables. Since 0.6.34

one graph's inventory row, by id: the row graph_inventory() has for it. Three answers that never look alike: the row (an empty graph shows 0), 42501 for a graph that exists and is not listed to the caller, and no row for a graph that does not exist. Since 0.6.42
one graph's inventory row, by IRI; same answers as the id form. A quoted number is read as an IRI: write graph_inventory(42) for the id. Since 0.6.42

portable manifest of one graph: three digests each carrying its method (bytes / rdfc-1.0 identity / fd1 structure), counts, engine identity, and what is NOT carried. Pair with export_graph to build a redistributable package. Since 0.6.41 every value describes the SET of asserted triples: counts.asserted is the number of export lines, counts.repeats appears only when the graph stores some triple more than once (the surplus rows), and consistent says whether the three passes are known to have read the same data (the graph is locked, or the transaction is REPEATABLE READ or stricter). Refuses like graph_digest (54000, 22021). Since 0.6.34
IRI bound to a graph_id, or NULL when unknown

per-call completeness figures (path_depth_truncations, filter_clauses_dropped) for the most recent sparql/construct/describe call in THIS session; session-local, so other sessions cannot pollute it. Read it right after the query. Since 0.6.34 Since 0.6.41 also `load`: the import report (read, stored, made asserted, dropped) when the most recent call was a loader, else null

column1: load_turtle(path text, graph_id bigint, base_iri text, bulk_load boolean)
column3: load a Turtle FILE from the server filesystem; bulk_load enables the parallel ingest fast path on an empty database (owner of pgrdf._pgrdf_quads only; any other role, or a populated database, loads through the standard path) . Returns the triples READ; a graph is a set, so repeated triples are not stored again (since 0.6.41): the counts are in load_turtle_verbose's `load` report, the load act and last_call_stats(). A term containing U+0000 refuses 22P05

staged-loader worker-pool liveness diagnostic

column3: staged multi-worker bulk load, function form; returns the run report. Since 0.6.41: stores a set (repeats in the file are removed when the graph's unique index is built), keeps blank-node subjects as blank nodes, registers the graph with its owner, records its load act with the caller's identity, and reports `load` and, on failure, the failing worker's `sqlstate`

column1: load_turtle_streaming(path text, graph_id bigint, window_triples integer, id_reserve_block integer, base_iri text)
column3: windowed streaming load for files larger than memory

column1: load_turtle_verbose(path text, graph_id bigint, base_iri text, bulk_load boolean)
column3: load_turtle returning a JSONB report (counts, timings, source sha256) instead of a bare count
write-fence a graph with a mandatory reason; every engine write path refuses while held (55P03). A coordination primitive, not a security boundary. Since 0.6.28

OWL 2 RL ('owl-rl') or RDFS ('rdfs') forward-chaining entailment; wipes and rewrites the graph's inferred rows; unknown profile refuses (22023) . An inferred triple never duplicates or changes a stored one. Refuses 54000 before reading a graph larger than pgrdf.max_inmemory_triples when that is set. Recorded as a materialize act (since 0.6.41)
move src into an EMPTY dst and drop src; non-empty dst refuses (55000)
move by IRI; same empty-destination requirement
quad partitions with no registered graph — invisible to SPARQL and to graph-level export/digest; a non-empty result deserves investigation. Since 0.6.34

storage objects (tables, partitions, standalone sequences, the pgrdf schema) not owned by the storage owner, the owner of pgrdf._pgrdf_quads that graph creation, clear, drop, lock and the act record run as; blocking is true exactly when that owner lacks what the engine does on the object as that role (a partition: ownership; _pgrdf_graphs: SELECT and UPDATE; _pgrdf_graph_acts: INSERT; the two id sequences; the schema: USAGE and CREATE; anything else is listed and never blocking), cure gives the statement that realigns each. Empty when ownership agrees. Since 0.6.40; per-object rule and the schema row since 0.6.41

column1: parse_nquads(content text, default_graph_id bigint, strict boolean)
column3: parse N-Quads text; quads without a graph label land in default_graph_id

column1: parse_trig(content text, default_graph_id bigint, strict boolean)
column3: parse TriG text; triples outside named graphs land in default_graph_id

column1: parse_turtle(content text, graph_id bigint, base_iri text)
column3: parse Turtle text into a graph; returns the triples READ. A graph is a set: a triple it already holds is not stored again (since 0.6.41); the stored and dropped counts are in parse_turtle_verbose's `load` report, the load act and last_call_stats()

column1: parse_turtle_dict_batched(content text, graph_id bigint, base_iri text, dict_batch_size integer)
column3: tuning variant of parse_turtle with explicit dictionary batching; use parse_turtle

column1: parse_turtle_verbose(content text, graph_id bigint, base_iri text)
column3: parse_turtle returning a JSONB report instead of a bare count. Since 0.6.41 it carries `load`: triples_read, parse_skipped, triples_stored, inferred_made_asserted, duplicates_dropped, graph_was_empty
drop this backend's prepared-plan cache; a diagnostic, not part of any workflow
ingest one CONSTRUCT-shaped JSONB row; the round-trip partner of construct()
ingest CONSTRUCT-shaped JSONB rows in bulk; the round-trip partner of construct() . Stores a set; a language tag is stored in lower case, as the parsers store it (since 0.6.41)

column1: put_quad(s bigint, p bigint, o bigint, g bigint)
column3: raw quad insert by dictionary ids; bypasses parsing and the act record. A triple the graph already holds is not stored again (since 0.6.41)
raw dictionary insert; returns the term id
warm the shared term cache from the dictionary after a restart or shmem_reset

invalidate the shared term cache (bumps its generation). Needed after DROP/CREATE EXTENSION in a live cluster. The historic use — clearing subtransaction-abort poisoning — is fixed since 0.6.33 and no longer requires this . Not PUBLIC since 0.6.41: superusers and the extension owner only

SPARQL SELECT/ASK and UPDATE; rows are JSONB bindings. Pair with last_call_stats() for per-call completeness; no GRAPH clause means the union of all graphs . Since 0.6.41 an UPDATE reports the triples it actually stored (not the ones it was asked to store), records one update act per graph it changed, and refuses with a typed SQLSTATE (0A000 unsupported shape, 42601 parse error, 42704 / 42710 / 22023 request error, 54000 limit); COPY, ADD and MOVE from a graph that does not exist refuse 42704
parse-only dry run: the algebra, or what the engine cannot run, without executing
translation dry run: the SQL a query would execute
synthetic ingest benchmark (flat table variant); measurement harness, not API
synthetic ingest benchmark (indexed variant); measurement harness, not API
synthetic ingest benchmark (partitioned variant); measurement harness, not API
synthetic ingest benchmark sweeping batch sizes; measurement harness, not API

instance-wide health counters (caches, truncations, filter refusals). Cumulative and global — never a per-call verdict; use last_call_stats() for that . Not PUBLIC since 0.6.41: GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION pgrdf.stats() TO a monitoring role

first-degree structural pin, method pgrdf-fd1-sha256 — the cross-implementation interop digest. Unequal values PROVE difference; equal values are evidence, not proof. Use graph_digest for conclusive identity; the two methods' values are never comparable. Over the SET of asserted triples: a triple stored more than once counts once (since 0.6.41). Absent graph refuses (42704); more blank-node triples than pgrdf.digest_max_bnode_quads refuses 54000; a term with U+0000 refuses 22021. Since 0.6.34
this listing: every export with its stability class. Ask the engine what it supports instead of probing function existence. Since 0.6.34
release a graph lock with a mandatory reason — the cure the lock refusal names. Unlocking an unlocked graph refuses (55000). Since 0.6.28

column1: validate(data_graph_id bigint, shapes_graph_id bigint, mode text, strict boolean)
column3: SHACL validation report (modes: native, sparql, pgrdf). The report payload shape is frozen — tooling may rely on it. Since 0.6.41 each call that answers is one validate act on the data graph (see graph_acts) and the report adds act_recorded, act_id and, when nothing was recorded, act_reason: an unregistered data graph or a read-only transaction records nothing. With pgrdf.max_inmemory_triples set, a call that would read more triples (data plus shapes) refuses 54000 before reading
extension version; with build_id() and pg_extension.extversion forms the identity triple a healthy deployment shows as three equal values

which SHACL features validate enforces, one row per feature of SHACL Core; verdict is enforced / not enforced / unprobed, and unprobed features are listed rather than omitted so the row count is the denominator. Since 0.6.35

trigger function on the act record: refuses every direct INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE (42501) unless the writer holds the table owner's privileges, so the record is written by the engine only. Not callable as an API. Since 0.6.41

backends inside a pgRDF graph-level act right now, in this database (write acts, whole-graph reads, validation), with graph, act, start time and the acting and declared identity. Reports, never blocks. Follows pg_stat_activity visibility: another role's session shows only pid and session_role unless the caller holds that role's privileges or pg_read_all_stats. Needs shared_preload_libraries. Since 0.6.41

column1: graph_acts(graph_id bigint, since timestamp with time zone)
column3: the act record: one row per committed graph-level act (create, rename, load, update, ingest, clear, drop, copy, move, carve, lock, unlock, materialize, validate, set_owner), never per triple. Each row keeps the verified identity (session_role, acting_role) apart from the declared one (application_name, requester, workspace, agent, thread, on_behalf_of, harness), with the transaction id and a detail object (counts, lock reason, source; for validate the verdict, result count, mode, the shapes graph's id, IRI and digest, and the data graph's materialization state). Both arguments are optional filters. Since 0.6.41

hand a graph to another role; allowed for the current owner and the storage owner, and recorded as an act. The owner is a pgRDF record (a role name), not a PostgreSQL relation owner. It gates the destructive acts only when pgrdf.graph_owner_enforce is on. Since 0.6.41

builds the unique subject-predicate-object index on one partition of the quad table; when the build finds repeated rows it either removes the surplus first (dedup true) or builds a plain index and leaves the partition unconstrained (dedup false). Used by graph creation's siblings, the bulk and staged loaders, dedup_graph and the upgrade. Since 0.6.41

remove the repeated rows of a graph loaded before 0.6.41 and build its unique index; returns the surplus rows removed. Keeps an asserted row over an inferred one, so the set of triples and a current materialization are unchanged. Refuses a locked graph (55P03). Recorded as a dedup act. Since 0.6.41

graphs whose partition does not carry the unique index, with rows, distinct_rows, surplus, groups and max_multiplicity, lock state and a note naming the cure; plus one row with graph_id NULL when the dictionary holds a term under more than one id. Scans only unconstrained partitions: empty on a healthy database. Since 0.6.41
trigger function on the stored-count delta table: a delta is accepted only from the engine's own write statement, so a direct INSERT refuses 42501. Since 0.6.42

trigger function on the quad table and its partitions: a write that did not come through the engine's writer marks the stored count of the graph it names unverified (every graph, when the statement names the parent) until pgrdf.recount_graph. Since 0.6.42

count a graph again and store what the scan finds: the cure for a count that is not verified (counts_verified false in graph_inventory), which is what a write made in plain SQL, a restore from a dump, or a privileged role that switched the count triggers off leaves behind. Returns the count found beside the count that was stored and whether that one was verified. recount_graph(NULL) does it for every graph listed to the caller, one row each. Changes no triple, so it runs on a locked graph; recorded as act recount. Refuses 42501 for a graph not listed to the caller and 42704 for one that does not exist. Since 0.6.42

one row of totals over the graphs listed to the caller: scope ('all' for an admin, 'own' for any other role), graphs_listed, graphs_total (the number of graphs in the database, for every caller, so a client can tell "not listed to me" from "dropped"), asserted, inferred, unverified_graphs (listed graphs that had to be counted by scan for this call) and terms (dictionary terms; NULL when the scope is 'own', because the dictionary belongs to the database). Since 0.6.42

column1: graph_act_feed(after xid8, only_graph bigint, page text, max_acts integer)
column3: the act record as a feed a poller can trust: acts ordered by transaction, with one cursor, complete_below, meaning everything below it has been delivered in full. Keep it and pass it as after on the next call; drop act ids already seen. A visible act is committed and is never tentative; only the window above the cursor is open. When more than max_acts remain, next_page is set: call again with page = next_page until it is NULL, then keep complete_below. Always returns at least one row; a row whose act_id is NULL carries the cursor and is not an act. Acts of the caller's own open transaction are left out. The cursor is held back by the oldest transaction running on the server. graph_acts() cannot be polled safely: it filters on the time a row was written, and an act whose transaction commits later is skipped. Since 0.6.42
